title: Strict etale functorial log blowup procedures
statement: For locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], call an input admissible if its underlying scheme is quasi-compact and every geometric characteristic group completion is torsion free. Call an input charted if it admits a global fan chart [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup]. A tower over an input is a finite saturated log blowup tower with its initial level identified with that input. A contracted pullback comparison over a log morphism is the recursive pullback of its ordered tower, with pulled-back log ideals as centers, followed by deletion of exactly the centers equal to the whole log monoid sheaf. Formally a monotone count map records the retained stages; an ordered embedding lists all and only those retained stages. Its level maps and repeated-level transition maps form fs Cartesian squares; retained transitions and centers are those of the source tower, and deleted transitions are log identities. A strict etale log blowup procedure on a class of inputs assigns such a tower to every member and such a comparison to every strict etale morphism between members. The comparison count maps and log maps satisfy the identity and composition laws. An isomorphism of towers over the same input is an ordered levelwise log isomorphism, the identity at the initial level, preserving all arrows and actual centers. Agreement of two procedures on a subdomain consists of these isomorphisms, natural for every strict etale comparison. Taking the domain to be all charted admissible inputs makes the assignment independent of a chosen fan chart and includes finite disjoint unions and their component inclusions.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.3.8--3.3.15, pp.108--110: towers, contraction, recursive pullback, and the functorial descent reduction.
